# secureworkload Provider

This provider can be used to manage the Secure Workload configuration.

## Features

You can manage the following resources with this provider:

- Workspace
- Scope
- Filter
- Label
- User
- Role
- Clusters
- Policies & Ports
- Policy Enforcement

Further, the provider provides the below data sources:

- Scope
- Cluster
- Filter
- Role
- Scope
- Workspace

## Example

An example provider initialization is shown below:

```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    secureworkload = {
      source = "CiscoDevNet/secureworkload"
    }
  }
}

provider "secureworkload" {
    api_key                  = "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"
    api_secret               = "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"
    api_url                  = "https://acme.secureworkloadpreview.com"
    disable_tls_verification = false
  }
```

**Note** You should use the terraform variables to supply the credentials securely.

## Upgrading from 1.8.0 to 1.8.1

Back up your state file before you upgrade.

In 1.8.0 the `secureworkload_port` resource stored the ID of the parent policy instead of the ID of the service port, and `secureworkload_enforce` stored the enforcement epoch instead of the workspace ID. Both are corrected in 1.8.1, and the state of existing resources is migrated automatically the first time you run `terraform plan` or `terraform apply`.

The migration only goes one way. Once you have applied with 1.8.1, version 1.8.0 will refuse to read the state of those two resources and reports `Resource instance managed by newer provider version`. Restoring a state backup is the only way back, so take one first.

Run `terraform plan` before `terraform apply`. A plan does not write state, so you can check the result first. For `secureworkload_port` and `secureworkload_enforce` you should see no changes.

A few resources also behave differently now:

- `secureworkload_policies` is no longer destroyed and recreated on every run.
- `secureworkload_workspace` updates `name`, `description` and `primary` in place.
- `secureworkload_role` updates `name` and `description` in place instead of being recreated.
- `secureworkload_scope` now recreates the scope when `policy_priority` changes. In 1.8.0 that change was silently applied by deleting and recreating the scope.

## Schema

### Required

- **api_key** (String) API key for calculating request signatures for SecureWorkload API calls.
- **api_secret** (String) API secret for calculating request signatures for SecureWorkload API calls.
- **api_url** (String) URL for a SecureWorkload API.

### Optional

- **disable_tls_verification** (Boolean) Allow connections to SecureWorkload endpoints without validating their TLS certificate.
- **max_retries** (Number) Number of attempts made for each API call before giving up. Requests that fail with HTTP 429 or a 5xx error are retried with a backoff, honouring the `Retry-After` header when the API sends one. Defaults to 5. Can also be set with the `SECUREWORKLOAD_MAX_RETRIES` environment variable.
- **http_timeout** (Number) Timeout in seconds for each API call attempt. Prevents a request from hanging indefinitely if the cluster stops responding. Defaults to 120. Can also be set with the `SECUREWORKLOAD_HTTP_TIMEOUT` environment variable.
